title: God Sees the Heart Behind Everything
overview: A loose collection of short sayings about motives, honesty, work, home life and humility, framed by the belief that the LORD sees the heart and has the final word.

parts.label: The LORD weighs motives (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The king's heart is pictured as irrigation water a farmer steers into channels, so even the most powerful person is under God's direction. People excuse their own choices, but God weighs the motives underneath, and fair dealing counts for more than animal offerings at the temple.

parts.label: Pride, haste and dishonest gain (vv. 4-8)
parts.note: Pride is called the 'lamp' or 'unplowed field' of the wicked (the Hebrew is unclear), meaning arrogance is what drives wrongdoing. Patient planning pays off, while rushing, lying and violence bring gains that vanish like mist and end up trapping the people who chase them.

parts.label: Trouble at home and next door (vv. 9-13)
parts.note: The saying about a quarrelsome wife (repeated in v. 19) speaks from a husband's view in an ancient household: constant conflict makes even a big house worse than a cramped corner of the flat roof. Nearby sayings warn about people who crave harm or mock correction, and say that whoever ignores the cry of the poor will one day cry for help and not be heard.

parts.label: Bribes, justice and ruin (vv. 14-19)
parts.note: Verse 14 simply observes that a hidden gift calms anger, and since Proverbs elsewhere condemns bribes that twist justice, it reads as a blunt observation rather than advice. The line about the wicked becoming a 'ransom' for the good probably means disaster lands on the wrongdoer instead of the innocent, though its exact sense is debated.

parts.label: Wise habits, foolish appetites (vv. 20-26)
parts.note: The wise save while fools gulp everything down, and the lazy person who wants much but will not work is ruined by his own cravings. Those who pursue goodness and kindness, guard their tongues and give freely find life, and clear thinking can even bring down a fortified city.

parts.label: The last word is God's (vv. 27-31)
parts.note: Religious offerings from someone set on wrongdoing are offensive to God, and a lying witness in court will come to ruin. Whatever plans people make or warhorses they prepare, the chapter ends by saying the outcome rests with the LORD.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether sayings like these (that diligence brings plenty and goodness brings life and honor) are promises God guarantees or general patterns of life that often, but not always, hold true.
think: When you judge your own choices, what helps you tell the difference between being right and just feeling right?
